summary: Krishnanath Chatterjee worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya (attested 1980).

Kristen De Joseph specializes in Indology. She studied under Arlo Griffiths (attested 2009) and pursued a self-funded PhD at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).

Kristin Johnston Largen works in religious and Buddhist studies. Her attested posts in 2018 include Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Colby College (BA), Harvard Divinity School (MTS), and Harvard University (PhD, 2006), working with Charles Hallisey, John S. Strong, Diana L. Eck, and Anne E. Monius. She held teaching posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold specializes in religious studies and Indology. She was an editor (attested 2005) and PhD candidate (attested 2008) at Lund University, and later served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Kristofer Schipper (1934–2021) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. Educated at École du Louvre, INALCO, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University, he held posts at EFEO, EPHE, CNRS, Collège de France, Leiden University, and Fuzhou University.

Krisztina Teleki (born 1978) specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), where she later served as a research fellow (~2011).
Kshanika Saha specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Nalinaksha Dutt and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966).

Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya (1896–1974) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University under Ganganatha Jha. His career included posts at Allahabad University, National Sanskrit University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned an MA from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He served in the Chamba State Department of Education (~1904–1908) and held posts at Visva-Bharati University, including Adhyaksha (1953–1954).

K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the University of Kelaniya. He held posts at Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Calgary, and University of Hong Kong.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), Tokyo University of Literature and Science (1943), University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).

Kumja Paik Kim (born 1934) specializes in art history and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate at Stanford University and served as curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum beginning in 1989.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay is an archaeology and history researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay. As of 2026, she is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua and Yale under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang. He held posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and the University of California, Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara, and served as Associate Professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1993).
Kunio Iwaya (born 1943) studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1964 to 1971. He held an academic post at Meiji Gakuin University from ~1978 to 2014.

Kunio Mugitani (born 1948) works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He served as a professor at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities (~1993–2012).
Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1928 to 1931. He later held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a religious studies and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, the Permanent Mandates Commission, the Privy Council, and Kokugakuin University.
